fixes.explanation: Good guess, friend, but not here. Psalm 57:1 never mentions Jonathan. David says, "…in You my soul takes refuge." and the "You" is God, since he opens with "Have mercy on me, O God…"

Yes, baker. David says he lies down "…with men whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords." Those are his words for how sharp and cutting these men are. I think that's one tough crowd to be among.
Ha, I'd be tempted to run too, baker. But David doesn't say that. With his heart steadfast, he says, "I will sing and make music."
Yes, baker. David says, "Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre!" The harp and lyre are the ones he calls on to wake up. I think that's a man ready to make music.
